# Process Names

**Summary**: Names for processes/actions that objects and phenomena undergo, generated by nominalizing verbs; paired with property names to form process quantities.

**Sources**: Peckham_and_Stoica_2022_ICWRER_2022.pdf

**Last updated**: 2026-06-06

---

Objects and phenomena often participate in or are subject to a **process** or action. For example, a glacier can melt, slide, sublimate, retreat, or calve — things described with verbs (source: Peckham_and_Stoica_2022_ICWRER_2022.pdf).

## Process Name Rule

Virtually all English process names are generated by **nominalizing a verb** (converting an action word to a noun), almost always by changing the word ending. Common endings (source: Peckham_and_Stoica_2022_ICWRER_2022.pdf):

| Ending | Examples |
|---|---|
| tion | absorption, convection, infiltration |
| sion | avulsion, conversion, dispersion |
| ing | melting, swimming, upwelling |
| age | drainage, seepage, storage |
| y | discovery, recovery |
| ance | acceptance, governance, maintenance |
| ment | alignment, improvement, recruitment |

This mirrors the [[property-names]] Property Name Rule (nominalizing adjectives).

## Process quantities

We frequently quantify an aspect of a process (its rate, the temperature at which it occurs, its frequency, etc.). This is very often done by **pairing a process name with a simple property name** to create a **process quantity** — an extremely common pattern (source: Peckham_and_Stoica_2022_ICWRER_2022.pdf).

Examples: dilution ratio, drainage area, escape speed, gestation period, inclination angle, inflation pressure, penetration depth, relaxation time, striking distance, turning radius, vibration frequency. For "ing" process names, the ending is often dropped: burn, creep, flow, lapse, melt, shear, tilt (e.g., melt rate, shear stress) (source: Peckham_and_Stoica_2022_ICWRER_2022.pdf).

Process quantities contrast with **state quantities**, which describe the state of an object/phenomenon (its mass, temperature, or any measure of its size) (source: Peckham_and_Stoica_2022_ICWRER_2022.pdf).
